title: Bandit & RL Setting Atlas
scope: Canonical working taxonomy for BanditRLlib. It separates mathematical settings from objectives, algorithm families, cross-cutting properties, and application bridges. It is a coverage baseline, not a claim that every named variant in the literature is exhausted.

policy.setting: Changes the admissible environment, action space, feedback, reward law, interaction, or resource model.
policy.objective: Changes what the learner is asked to optimize or identify.
policy.method: Algorithmic family that may cross several settings.
policy.cross-cutting: Property of guarantees or adaptation that can apply to several settings.
policy.application-bridge: Domain route whose mathematical contract must be mapped to one or more settings before bounds are compared.
policy.ambiguous: Community/user label whose expansion is not source-stable enough to canonicalize without a cited definition.

entries.title: Multi-Armed Bandits (MAB)
entries.summary: Finite-action bandit baseline; should be the root from which stochastic/adversarial and structured variants branch.

entries.title: Single-objective bandits
entries.summary: Scalar reward/regret objective; useful mainly as the parent contrast for multi-objective/Pareto bandits.

entries.title: Regret minimization
entries.summary: Cumulative learning objective; keep separate from pure exploration/identification.

entries.title: Best-arm identification (BAI)
entries.summary: Pure exploration, fixed-confidence or fixed-budget, with sample complexity/error probability rather than cumulative regret.

entries.title: Threshold / thresholding bandits
entries.summary: Identify/classify arms relative to a threshold; distinct from BAI despite sharing pure-exploration tools.

entries.title: Top-m / combinatorial pure exploration
entries.summary: Identify a subset or combinatorial optimum; important bridge between BAI and structured bandits.

entries.title: Model selection / corralling
entries.summary: Adapt to the best model/algorithm class without knowing its complexity in advance.

entries.title: Multi-objective / Pareto bandits
entries.summary: Vector rewards, scalarization or Pareto criteria; should not be hidden under single-objective MAB.

entries.title: Stochastic bandits
entries.summary: Stationary stochastic rewards; parent of many finite-arm and structured stochastic settings.

entries.title: Adversarial bandits
entries.summary: Adversarial loss/reward sequence with bandit feedback; a core setting missing as an explicit topic card.

entries.title: Semi-adversarial / best-of-both-worlds bandits
entries.summary: Algorithms adapt across stochastic/self-bounding/adversarial regimes; corruption is related but not identical.

entries.title: Corruption-tolerant bandits
entries.summary: Rewards/observations can be corrupted under an explicit adversary and corruption budget.

entries.title: Heavy-tailed bandits
entries.summary: Finite-moment rather than sub-Gaussian rewards; robust estimation and unknown-tail adaptation are central.

entries.title: Variance-aware bandits
entries.summary: Guarantees adapt to variance or second-order quantities rather than only range/sub-Gaussian proxies.

entries.title: Missing / censored outcome bandits
entries.summary: Selected rewards may be unobserved or censored; missingness mechanism must be part of the model contract.

entries.title: Dueling / preference bandits
entries.summary: Pairwise/comparative feedback rather than scalar reward observations.

entries.title: Partial monitoring
entries.summary: General feedback maps subsuming full information and bandits; important for locating feedback-complexity boundaries.

entries.title: Risk-sensitive / CVaR / survival bandits
entries.summary: Optimize tail risk, safety probability, ruin/survival or other distributional criteria beyond expected reward.

entries.title: Contextual bandits
entries.summary: Actions are chosen conditional on observed contexts; realizability and policy/function classes must be explicit.

entries.title: Linear bandits
entries.summary: Mean reward is linear in action/context features; OFUL/self-normalized confidence is a canonical route.

entries.title: Generalized linear bandits (GLB)
entries.summary: Known link function applied to a linear predictor; assumptions on link derivatives and contexts matter.

entries.title: Lipschitz / continuum-armed bandits
entries.summary: Metric action spaces with Lipschitz reward structure; zooming/near-optimality dimension is a major proof route.

entries.title: Kernel / RKHS bandits
entries.summary: Nonparametric function class in an RKHS; information gain and online confidence are core quantities.

entries.title: Gaussian-process UCB (GP-UCB)
entries.summary: A method for GP/RKHS bandits, not a separate setting; index it under kernel bandits and UCB methods.

entries.title: Bandit convex optimization
entries.summary: Bandit feedback for convex losses over convex action domains; now mature enough for a dedicated extended route.

entries.title: Combinatorial bandits
entries.summary: Combinatorial action sets, often with semi-bandit/full-bandit feedback; oracle/relaxation and computational hardness must be tracked.

entries.title: Matching bandits
entries.summary: Structured combinatorial actions defined by matchings; feedback and centralized/decentralized variants should be distinguished.

entries.title: Graph-feedback / graphical bandits
entries.summary: Feedback or reward structure is governed by a graph; distinguish feedback graphs from graph-structured reward models.

entries.title: Causal bandits
entries.summary: Actions/interventions interact with a causal model and possibly observational data.

entries.title: Matrix / low-rank / tensor bandits
entries.summary: Structured high-dimensional reward parameter; rank, action factorization and observation model must be explicit.

entries.title: Factored bandits
entries.summary: Reward/action model factorizes across components; distinguish from generic combinatorial and low-rank models.

entries.title: Unimodal / structured-order bandits
entries.summary: Means obey a unimodal/ordered structure that permits local exploration.

entries.title: Multinomial-logit (MNL) / assortment bandits
entries.summary: If 'multinomial' means MNL choice/assortment bandits, use this canonical label; a generic multinomial reward law is only a reward-distribution specialization.

entries.title: Sparse / high-dimensional bandits
entries.summary: Linear/GLM/kernel problems with sparsity or intrinsic-dimension structure; useful cross-pollination route to compressed sensing.

entries.title: Dynamic / nonstationary bandits
entries.summary: Reward model changes over time; variation, switch, drift and comparator budgets must not be conflated.

entries.title: Delayed-feedback bandits
entries.summary: Feedback arrives after delays; distinguish stochastic/adversarial and observable/anonymous delay models.

entries.title: Sleeping / availability bandits
entries.summary: Only a subset of arms is available each round.

entries.title: Ballooning / growing-arm bandits
entries.summary: The available arm set grows over time; the user's 'Bolling' label is normalized here to Ballooning.

entries.title: Rotting / rising / restless bandits
entries.summary: Rewards evolve with pulls or time; each subfamily needs its own dynamics contract.

entries.title: Constrained bandits
entries.summary: Actions/rewards are subject to resource, feasibility or long-run constraints.

entries.title: Bandits with knapsacks / budgeted bandits
entries.summary: Stochastic rewards consume resources; should be an explicit child of constrained/resource bandits.

entries.title: Safe bandits
entries.summary: Constraint violations themselves must be controlled; safety semantics differ from generic budget constraints.

entries.title: Multi-fidelity bandits
entries.summary: Queries trade fidelity/cost against information; connect to multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization.

entries.title: Batched / limited-adaptivity bandits
entries.summary: Feedback is only available between batches or the number of adaptive rounds is constrained.

entries.title: Parameter-free / adaptive bandits
entries.summary: Guarantees adapt to unknown horizon, scale, variation, tail or comparator complexity without prior tuning.

entries.title: Multi-agent bandits
entries.summary: Multiple learning agents with communication, collision, cooperation or competition contracts.

entries.title: Federated bandits
entries.summary: Distributed/federated clients learn with communication and heterogeneity constraints.

entries.title: Multi-bandit / multi-task bandits
entries.summary: Several related bandit tasks/instances are learned jointly; use only with a source-specific transfer/sharing model.

entries.title: Private / JDP bandits
entries.summary: Privacy constraints change achievable regret and proof techniques; currently has explicit COLT open-problem history.

entries.title: Fairness / incentives / strategic bandits
entries.summary: Learning interacts with fairness or strategic agent constraints; link to the economics/agents textbook routes.

entries.title: UCB / optimism methods
entries.summary: Confidence-bound method family crossing stochastic, linear, kernel and RL settings.

entries.title: Thompson sampling / posterior sampling
entries.summary: Bayesian/posterior-sampling method; keep as method, not setting.

entries.title: Elimination / successive rejects / racing
entries.summary: Core method family for pure exploration and confidence-based regret algorithms.

entries.title: EXP3 / FTRL / mirror-descent methods
entries.summary: Optimization-based adversarial-bandit methods and best-of-both-worlds variants.

entries.title: MDP reinforcement learning
entries.summary: Bandit-to-RL bridge; branch into episodic, discounted and average-reward objectives.

entries.title: Online / adversarial MDP
entries.summary: MDP with online/adversarial costs or changing environments; do not abbreviate as OMDP without expansion.

entries.title: Partially observable MDP (POMDP)
entries.summary: Partial observability changes planning and learning complexity.

entries.title: Offline / batch RL
entries.summary: Learn from a fixed dataset; coverage/concentrability replaces online exploration.

entries.title: Linear / kernel MDPs
entries.summary: Function-approximation RL routes; kernel RL has explicit COLT open-problem history.

entries.title: Constrained / safe RL
entries.summary: Sequential decision making under costs/safety constraints.

entries.title: Multi-agent RL
entries.summary: RL counterpart of multi-agent bandits; cooperative/competitive/game structure must be explicit.

entries.title: Bandits for LLM / language-model systems
entries.summary: Application bridge for preference learning, routing, inference-time allocation, evaluation or adaptation; map each paper back to a precise mathematical setting.

entries.title: OMDP
entries.summary: Do not canonicalize until a source defines whether this means online MDP, observable MDP, or another model.

entries.title: SLB
entries.summary: Likely intended as stochastic linear bandits in some usage, but require the collaborator's source before merging the acronym into that node.

entries.title: Transform
entries.summary: No stable canonical bandit setting was identified from the bare label; retain as an alias quarantine entry until a paper/source is supplied.
